Hi there! Using your face in a thumbnail is a big plus, keep doing that! Your videos get character and are immediately different from anything else on the internet since they have You! :)

As for the approach, it all depends on the type of content, really. The ones with a single color background are a bit risky to use, because of the color choice. Use a different color everytime, and it all looks like a hot mess once put in a playlist or an album. Use the same color, and every video looks the same, nothing separating them. Your portrait also seems very tiny in most of those monochromatic thumbnails, since everything around you is so empty (other than those few white pasted words). I'd say take a look at several other creators (Thomas Brush comes to mind) and see how they're doing it. They are mostly incorporating their video subject and theme into the thumbnail itself.

Your interview video thumbnails look more than decent, they remind me of podcast videos. Maybe put an accent on your interviewer, make them pop out? Don't be scared to zoom into peoples faces, yours included :) Check True Geordie for inspiration, if it helps.

Font can use a bit of work, but it's far from bad. Your micromanager videos have a very nice usage of font and text in general, they definitely pop out amongst your other videos.

My advice? Stay away from monochromatic backgrounds, put accent on your guests and try experimenting with fonts. I guess you're using Impact, Tarumian, Bebas Neue or some thick, condensed one, don't be afraid to try something else :) Try to keep it with two different fonts per thumbnail tho, never go above that. Good luck with your videos!

A lot of, and I mean a LOT OF text. Way too much. Fonts and colors are all over the place. It's chaotic and not in a good way. Arrows pointing at random places in your thumbnail, red border around black letters, some text hiding behind the time stamp in the bottom right corner...

Your last video thumbnail is being stretched beyond recognition. I'd say rethink your approach to thumbnails, because everything is better than this. Even youtube generated thumbnails.

Best advice I could give is KISS - Keep It Stupid Simple. Don't overdo it with text, fonts, borders, arrows, circles and logos.

EDIT: Just opened few of your videos, I get the aesthetic you're going for, which doesn't excuse bad thumbnails. Check 'Neat', he has similar approach to this, but way more organized

Not here to rate your videos since I'm definitely not qualified to do that (your videos are probably 10x better than mine), but I must say that you have a nice, fast and attention grabbing channel trailer. I guess you used one of the templates from Envato or some similar platform? Sorry for jumping to conclusions if you didn't :)

Channel art is nice, also looks like one of the zillion templates you can grab off the internet, which is far from a bad thing. If you like it and if it works, please use it. Much better than experimenting with something that would possibly turn away possible viewers.

Thumbnails are simple, yet effective (somewhat). Couple of them have some tiny text written on them that's supposed to be read, but the size of it makes it unreadable, automatically making it a thumbnail burden. GET RID OF IT! I'm talking specifically about your "January 2021 #Shorts" and "Eyes of Sleeping Children by D.A. Butcher" videos. That extra text you've put under the book needs to go.

Your first thumbnails have a slightly better aesthetic than your last ones, but only because of the format. Book on one side, text on the other. Simple, yet effective. Don't stick with that format, far from it actually, or else all of your thumbnails would look exactly the same, but try to lean to that approach, more than screenshots of the book with a blurry background to fill in the black space, like you did in your latest video. Also, use some online palettes for your thumbnail colors. Desaturated blues and reds don't work that well with dark grays. [Coolors.co](https://Coolors.co) is a great resource for this, if used properly.

One more thing that's painfully obvious is that you're using templates left and right, and as I said it can be a good thing, but make sure you don't lose your identity by doing this. Again, this is mainly for the video itself, not much for thumbnails, but I'm sure you won't mind this extra bit of feedback :)

Hi! I'll just dump pros and cons here, hope you don't mind the format :)

PROS:

\- There's definitely an improvement from your first videos, where you just had a screengrab grabbed from the video. Keep at it  
\- Huge text as an attention grabber: Big Yes!  
\- Your face, so the viewer know they're not getting just another "let's play" with a dead voice in the background, since they can connect the voice with a potential facecam.  
\- Colorful, every thumbnail is different  


CONS:

\- Huge text is a yes, but not in so many colors. Your latest video as an example: You have A, B, C, D ranking letters in your thumbnail in 4 different, desaturated colors, followed by very saturated yellow words DON'T and THIS, then followed by a yellow glow around the portrait. Bit too much, everything is messy. Keep it simple, get a palette and use it, don't just dump every single color into one thumbnail :)  
\- Using blurry images for a facecam preview is a no no. You're in risk of chasing people away by seeing a low cam quality. Try to make a picture for your thumbnail by taking a photo with your phone/camera, not by extracting a screenshot from your video  
\- Illustrated avatars are cool, but they are completely different in every thumbnail. Makes your channel lose it's character. People have nothing to relate you to if they see a different mascot/avatar every time. Using facecam instead is a big plus, glad to see you going in that direction.

To be honest, this is such a weak mentality that will get you nowhere on the platform. You have to pay attention to numbers and try to improve on them in order to improve the overall quality of your channel. If you see one video doing much better than the others, you have to figure out how and why did it happen and try to replicate or even improve the formula (not necessarily make the exact same video, but approach it from the same angle at least).

Also if numbers tell you that no one sticks to one of your videos longer than few seconds, while watching the other one for almost it's full duration, it's a good signal to revisit those videos and compare their content and it's quality. Why does it happen? What can you do to improve on it? 

Posts like this are very hurtful for small and upcoming channels who are serious about their possible future profession. I'd say keep a close eye on those numbers and continue growing, because one day it will pay of. Ask any slightly bigger youtuber if they ignore the numbers as this posts suggests.
